BUY: Kratos Defense sourced from the standard watchlist screen (quant score driven by 30.5% revenue growth). No negative catalysts found -- FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $1.75-1.81B on 19.1% organic growth (Q2, 8/4), plus new contract wins (~$35M hardware award, $20M+ SATCOM gateway deal) and a successful ARAV-B missile-target test (9/9); hypersonics unit guided to ~$400M revenue in 2026, $700M+ in 2027. Passed again on the two highest-scoring screen candidates, RCAT and SERV: RCAT still carries a governance overhang (its CRO, not CEO as initially flagged, was terminated 'for Cause' 7/23 and has since sued for retaliation; heavy CEO insider selling on 9/15; steep downtrend) and SERV's FY26 revenue-guidance cut ($26M to $9-10M on Uber Eats weakness) and customer-concentration risk both still stand as of 9/22. Also passed on HIMS (opportunity-tier, decent growth but an active new investor class-action lawsuit plus FDA compounded-GLP-1 warnings and Visa dispute-monitoring -- too much fresh legal/regulatory overhang for the size of the opportunity), LEU (a dilutive $500M share offering just hit the stock, in the middle of digesting that news), and META (up 11.4% in a single day on the Muse app-store pop heading into Meta Connect -- momentum-chasing entry, not a value-conscious one). Opportunity-tier (~$8.8B market cap); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor (~$20.11), the binding constraint today (ample remaining room in both the Industrials sector cap and the opportunity bucket).

Modine Manufacturing sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (AI data-center liquid-cooling/thermal management). FY26 net sales +23% YoY to $3.2B, driven by a 90% increase in data-center cooling revenue, and the company signed a new long-term agreement this week to supply over $4B in cooling products through 2029 -- multi-year revenue visibility. Forward P/E 16.8 with 28% revenue growth and 44% earnings growth is a reasonable growth-at-a-reasonable-price setup versus richer AI-infra peers (e.g. RKLB's ~1,489x forward P/E, screened but passed on for this reason). Opportunity-tier (market cap ~$9.8B, just under the $10B threshold); sized to the full remaining opportunity-bucket room (~$23, bucket already ~19.4% of its 20% cap) rather than a full position, funded by available cash above the 2% buffer floor.

AST SpaceMobile sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (direct-to-cell satellite connectivity). Shifting from proof-of-concept to commercial activation: BlueBird 11-13 satellites deployed, new New Zealand gateway opened, deepening carrier integration (Vodafone/Orange/Telefonica/Deutsche Telekom via a gateway JV) and US Mobile preparing a direct-to-cell launch. 2026 revenue guided to $150-200M (vs. a near-zero prior-year base, which drove the quantitative screen's outsized revenue-growth score), backed by a $1.3B backlog and over $3.7B cash funding the buildout. Key risk is execution on an expensive, tightly-timed deployment (implied ~165%/yr revenue growth needed through 2029), but the bull case is still considered intact by sell-side (~$78 fair-value estimate vs. ~$59.27 entry). Not opportunity-tier (~$23B market cap). Sized to the remaining Technology sector-cap room (~$81.65, sector already ~28% of portfolio) rather than a full position; funded by today's VRT trim proceeds.

No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation; Q2 organic-growth guidance was actually raised to a 20-22% CAGR target through 2030, and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 average PT, GLJ upgrade to Buy $381). Trimming 30% to de-risk specifically because the 9/9 $1.45B UtilityInnovation Group acquisition still has undisclosed target financials and the Massachusetts data-center permitting order remains an unresolved overhang layered on top of the high beta -- not a full exit since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.
